The tables above answer the two questions that always come up: which services the ad money buys, and which searches it goes to. Three things stand out. Brand searches, people already looking for Smith Bros, convert for a few dollars each and carry most of the search conversions. Tint is the strongest non-brand service and already earns its share of spend. And the broad detailing terms, led by the most expensive keyword in the account, buy plenty of clicks that do not become bookings, while PPF is barely advertised at all. Rebalancing toward tint is already in the work queue; PPF needs a decision on whether it gets its own campaign.

What grid tracking measures

Rank on Google Maps is not one number. Where you show up in the map pack changes depending on where the searcher is standing. So instead of checking rank from a single point, we scan a grid of points around the location and record your position at every one. Three numbers come out of that scan.

  • ARP: average position across the points where you show up.
  • ATRP: average position across every point in the grid, counting the points where you do not show up as misses.
  • SoLV: the percentage of the area where you land in the top 3.
